summary: Gross hepatobiliary specimen with progressive organ, duct-outlet, circulation and peritoneal relationship views. Named cameras restore geometry framing, exact selector visibility and clipping status; opacity and liver-lift recipes require explicit slider application. The four surface lobes are not a functional segment map.
scale_note: Gross schematic specimen; 1 unit is approximately 10 cm. Smaller duct and arterial calibres are exaggerated for visibility by an unspecified factor. Camera zoom is not an anatomical enlargement or a patient measurement.

01 Whole specimen.note: Locate liver, gallbladder, pancreatic head in the duodenal C-loop and the major route families at native default 50% tissue opacity. Set Tissue opacity to 50% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

02 Opaque organ survey.note: Show the gross organ silhouette and intentional D2 specimen window before tracing inner routes. Set Tissue opacity to 100% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

03 Visceral liver and porta.note: Identify the entrance/exit region with liver surface retained; distinguish ducts, arteries and portal vein. Set Tissue opacity to 35% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

04 Liver lifted teaching arrangement.note: Lift rank-marked liver structures to expose relationships beneath the liver; explain the artificial separation. Set Tissue opacity to 65% and Separate layers to 70 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

05 Cystic junction.note: Follow the gallbladder side branch joining the displayed common hepatic/common bile route. Set Tissue opacity to 100% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

06 Pancreatic ducts in context.note: Trace main and accessory pancreatic ducts while retaining the pancreatic head, uncinate/neck region and duodenal loop. Set Tissue opacity to 28% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

07 Papillae in opened D2.note: Distinguish the intentional front D2 window from the actual major papillary opening and retain minor outlet context. Set Tissue opacity to 70% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

08 Ampullary outlet with cuff hidden.note: Follow the displayed convergence and outlet within the surrounding D2/papillary wall. Set Tissue opacity to 30% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

09 Sphincter relationship.note: Compare the muscle surrounding the outlet with the preceding cuff-hidden route view. Set Tissue opacity to 30% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

10 Portal inflow in context.note: Follow splenic/mesenteric tributaries to portal inflow without superimposing hepatic venous drainage. Set Tissue opacity to 20% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

11 Hepatic venous outflow.note: Follow hepatic venous drainage toward the IVC, separate from portal inflow. Set Tissue opacity to 20% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

12 Arterial routes in context.note: Retain gross context while following the aortic, coeliac and named hepatic/pancreatic-region arterial routes. Set Tissue opacity to 20% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

13 Posterior peritoneal landmarks.note: Relate coronary/triangular peritoneal reflections to the posterior bare-area location. Set Tissue opacity to 100% and Separate layers to 0 using the sliders or explicit recipe adapter; camera buttons do not set these controls.

F01 Liver produces bile.note: Hepatocytes actively secrete bile constituents into canaliculi; osmotic water movement contributes to bile formation. Canaliculi and canals of Hering are unmodeled here; the named hepatic ducts show the gross exit. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F02 Ducts modify and carry bile.note: Cholangiocytes add bicarbonate-rich fluid, with secretin-responsive transport. Duct epithelium and its transporters are explained in text rather than added to this gross specimen. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 25%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F03 Gallbladder stores and concentrates.note: Between meals, downstream resistance favors entry through the cystic duct into the gallbladder. Water and electrolyte absorption concentrates stored bile. This is a predominant storage state, not a claim of zero duodenal flow or a tightly shut valve. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 25%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F04 Meal-associated bile release.note: Nutrients stimulate CCK-related regulation: gallbladder smooth muscle contracts and sphincter resistance falls. Bile exits through the same cystic duct toward the common bile duct, ampulla and major papilla into D2. The cystic duct has bidirectional use across states. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 25%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F05 Inspect the route through the papill.note: Hide the sphincter selector only to expose the outlet. This visibility action does not depict relaxation. The shared ampullary arrangement is representative and variable in individuals; the intentional D2 specimen window differs from the actual papillary opening. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 25%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F06 Acid enters the proximal duodenum.note: Acidic chyme stimulates duodenal S cells to release secretin into blood. Secretin acts on pancreatic ductal cells; cholinergic inputs contribute. S cells and hormone travel are unmodeled. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F07 Ductal bicarbonate and water.note: Secretin signaling raises duct-cell cAMP; CFTR-associated apical anion transport and chloride/bicarbonate exchange support bicarbonate secretion. Sodium and water follow electrical/osmotic gradients. Ductular secretion carries acinar products toward the intestine. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F08 Nutrients increase enzyme secretion.note: Fat and protein digestion products stimulate intestinal CCK-related hormonal and vagovagal pathways. Acinar cells have basal rough ER and apical secretory granules; the gross head/body/tail selectors are context, not separate secretion compartments. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F09 Two secretory functions share ductal.note: Duct fluid transports digestive enzymes to the duodenum. Bicarbonate helps provide a suitable pH for their activity. The accessory duct and minor papilla remain separately identifiable; this specimen does not establish individual duct configuration. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F10 Portal inflow from abdominal organs.note: Trace superior mesenteric and splenic contributions toward the hepatic portal vein, posterior to the pancreatic neck. The inferior mesenteric tributary retains its depicted insertion. This portal blood brings absorbed substances to the liver; it is not oxygen-free. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F11 Hepatic arterial supply.note: Follow the abdominal aorta, coeliac trunk, common hepatic artery and hepatic artery proper to right and left hepatic arteries. These provide the second, more oxygenated inflow. The schematic calibres do not encode relative blood-flow fractions. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F12 Explain the unmodeled exchange bed.note: Portal and arterial branches feed sinusoids; blood mixes and passes toward central veins. This microscopic exchange bed is absent from the gross specimen. Do not add a direct portal-to-hepatic-vein tube to connect visible gaps. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F13 Hepatic venous drainage.note: Central venous drainage converges into hepatic veins and then the IVC. Compare this exit with portal entry. The named hepatic-veins selector represents the drainage network; vessel crossings must not be taught as junctions. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F14 Three neighboring routes at the port.note: Compare hepatic portal vein and hepatic arterial entry with right/left hepatic duct exit. Proximity does not mean luminal communication; these selectors preserve independent passage systems. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 25%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F15 Microscopic directions differ.note: In lobular teaching, blood passes from portal-region inflow toward central venous outflow; bile produced by hepatocytes drains toward portal-region ducts. This model shows gross trunks only. Open the separately reviewed liver-lobule model for microscopic orientation; do not map its scale onto this specimen. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 25%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F16 Bile supports lipid digestion and ab.note: Bile salts disperse lipids and help solubilize digestion products. They do not replace pancreatic digestive enzymes. Follow delivery through the major papilla into the proximal intestinal lumen. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.

F17 Ileal reabsorption and portal return.note: Most bile acids are reabsorbed distally in the ileum and return through portal blood for hepatic uptake and resecretion. The ileum and its absorption machinery are absent. This transition is text-only; the shown jejunal cut end is not the ileal absorption site. Static qualitative teaching state. Set Tissue opacity to 50%; Separate layers to 0. No physical animation.
